about: Generator-side notes on must_show items (not part of the rule set). conditional: whether the item applies in some files only; applies_when: a condition over designed fact states that makes a conditional item required (if it does not hold, the item does not apply and is left out); checkable_as: what a document must literally contain for the item to count as shown, passed to the writer and to the blind checker; observed: the round-1 blind-check mismatch that led to the entry; rule_set_wording: why the item's own wording is a problem, for the planner to raise with the rule set (absent where the wording is fine).

items.item: the date (day, month and year) on which the theft was notified to CSS
items.checkable_as: The calendar date (day, month, year) on which the insurer was notified, and that the insurer is the addressee. A record that mentions the notification without its date does not show this item.
items.observed: 6 files designed missing, read sufficient (the_12ee892d56f4, the_1487759fc403, the_506c9909edc4, the_93929f818110, the_a86e098e517e, the_e0b1e1d56fb2)
items.rule_set_wording: The document's only item: a notification record that lacks it is not a notification record, so an insufficient copy is hard to write and to recognise; split into 'the date of notification' and 'the channel or addressee'.

items.item: for each item, where and when it was bought, or, for an item that was not bought, how and when it was acquired (for example as a gift or by inheritance)
items.checkable_as: For every listed item, the shop or seller and at least month and year of purchase, or, for an item that was not bought, how it was acquired (for example 'gift' or 'inherited', with the occasion) and when.
items.observed: 6 files designed sufficient read missing, 6 files read missing it in addition to the designed item (the generator had treated the item as conditional because it begins with 'where')
items.revision_3: Revision 3 (second look, 2026-11-12): any way of acquiring an item that was not bought, as the second reader worded it (R2-3).

items.rule_set_wording: The 'if' clause is a need condition (already in needed_when), not a content item.

items.item: Only if the file states that the policy includes the supplementary insurance for simple theft away (Ziff. 24.2): the sum insured agreed for that cover. Otherwise this item does not apply.
items.checkable_as: An amount in CHF labelled as the sum insured for the supplementary insurance for simple theft away (Ziff. 24.2), not the sum insured for household contents.
items.observed: the_d9579f891719: read missing in addition to the designed item
items.revision_3: Revision 3 (second look, 2026-11-12): ruling (b): the sum agreed for the simple-theft-away cover, conditional on the file stating that the cover is included (away_cover_missing stated false).

items.item: the complete list of the covers included in the policy (the supplementary insurance for simple theft away, Ziff. 24.2, is insured only if it is on that list)
items.checkable_as: The policy's complete list of the covers included (basic cover and every supplementary insurance taken out). Simple theft away from home (einfacher Diebstahl auswärts) is insured only if it is on that list; no 'not included' entry is required. An extract that shows only some covers, or no list of covers, does not show this item.
items.rule_set_wording: 'or its absence' lets a silent policy count as showing the item; better: 'whether the supplementary cover for simple theft away is listed as included or excluded'.
items.revision_3: Revision 3 (second look, 2026-11-12): complete list of covers, as the second reader worded it (R2-2).
